results.title: Completeness for the Clifford+T fragment
results.summary: The ZX-calculus with the rules of Fig. 1 is complete for the π/4-fragment (Clifford+T): two diagrams with angles multiple of π/4 are equal as matrices, scalars included, iff they can be rewritten into each other. All rules also hold upside-down and with the colours swapped.

axioms.label: (S3)
axioms.description: A bare cup (cap) equals a phase-free Z-spider with two outputs (inputs): wires can be bent.

axioms.label: (B1)
axioms.note: The scalar is written as a diagram.

axioms.label: (B2)
axioms.note: The paper writes the scalar √2 as a diagram (a connected Z/X pair); here it is stored as a number.

axioms.label: (K)
axioms.note: The paper's version has one input and one output, the colours swapped and the scalars written as diagrams; the stored rule copies an X(π) through a Z(α)-spider with two outputs, with scalar e^{iα} as a number.

axioms.label: (H)
axioms.note: The paper writes Hadamard gates on the legs of one of the spiders; here they are Hadamard edges.

results.title: ZX-calculus with parametrised triangles
results.summary: With a parametrised triangle Δ(r) (r ∈ ℂ) added as a generator, the rules ZX_Δ of Fig. 6 are complete for pure qubit quantum mechanics.

axioms.description: Triangle decomposition: for α ≠ π/2 mod π, the parametrised triangle with parameter e^{iθ}tan(α) equals a ZX-diagram in the angles α and θ (with a scalar).

axioms.label: (BW')
axioms.description: A triangle, a Z(π) phase and an upside-down triangle in sequence equal an X(π) phase followed by a triangle; replaces (BW).

axioms.label: (TA)
axioms.description: Triangle addition: two parametrised triangles in sequence, with parameters r and s, equal one triangle with parameter r+s.

results.title: Completeness with the Euler-angle rule
results.summary: The nine rules of Fig. 1, including the non-linear Euler-angle rule (EU), form a complete axiomatisation of the ZX-calculus for pure qubit quantum mechanics, scalars included. Along the way, the paper shows that the same set is complete for the π/2- and π/4-fragments.

results.title: Universal completion with triangle and λ-box
results.summary: With two extra generators, the triangle and the λ-box, the rules of Figs. 1–3 make the ZX-calculus complete for pure qubit quantum mechanics (scalars included). Upside-down versions of all rules also hold.

axioms.label: (S3)
axioms.description: A bare cup (cap) equals a phase-free Z-spider with two outputs (inputs): wires can be bent.

axioms.label: (H2)
axioms.note: The paper composes two Hadamard gates; here they are two Hadamard edges around a phase-free Z-spider.

axioms.label: (H3)
axioms.description: A Hadamard gate on one leg of a cap can be moved to the other leg.

axioms.label: (H)
axioms.note: The paper writes Hadamard gates on the legs of one of the spiders; here they are Hadamard edges.

axioms.label: (B1)
axioms.note: The scalar is written as a diagram.

axioms.label: (B2)
axioms.note: The paper writes the scalar √2 as a diagram (a connected Z/X pair); here it is stored as a number.

axioms.label: (EU)
axioms.note: The paper writes the scalar e^{-iπ/4} as diagrams (two triple-wire Z/X pairs and a connected X(-π/2)/Z(-π/2) pair); here it is stored as a number.

axioms.label: (K2)
axioms.note: The paper's version has one input and one output, the colours swapped and the scalars written as diagrams; the stored rule copies an X(π) through a Z(α)-spider with two outputs, with scalar e^{iα} as a number.

axioms.label: (S4)
axioms.note: Matches only up to representation: the paper's rule says a Z(α) phase followed by a phase-free X-effect equals the X-effect, i.e. the transposed one-leg case (a = 0) of the stored rule, which has two legs.

axioms.label: (IV)
axioms.description: A scalar built from a Z/X pair, a Z(π)-spider and a λ-box with label 1 − 1/√2 equals the empty diagram.

axioms.label: (L1)
axioms.description: A λ-box can be moved between the legs of a phase-free Z-spider.

axioms.label: (AD)
axioms.description: Addition rule: two branches carrying λ₁e^{iβ} and λ₂e^{iα} (λ-boxes and phases), joined by a W-like structure built from triangles, equal a single branch carrying λe^{iγ} where λe^{iγ} = λ₁e^{iβ} + λ₂e^{iα}.

axioms.label: (L2)
axioms.description: A λ-box followed by an X-effect equals the X-effect.

axioms.label: (L3)
axioms.description: A λ-box with label 1 is the identity.

axioms.label: (L4)
axioms.description: Two λ-boxes in sequence multiply: λ₁ then λ₂ equals λ₁·λ₂.

axioms.label: (L5)
axioms.description: A λ-box commutes with a Z(α) phase.

axioms.label: (TR1)
axioms.description: An upside-down triangle followed by X(π) equals X(π) followed by a triangle.

axioms.label: (TR2)
axioms.description: The triangle leaves the phase-free X-state unchanged.

axioms.label: (TR3)
axioms.description: The triangle applied to the X(π)-state gives the phase-free Z-state (with a scalar Z/X pair).

axioms.label: (TR4)
axioms.description: An upside-down triangle applied to the Z(π)-state gives the X-state (with a scalar Z/X pair).

axioms.label: (TR5)
axioms.description: A Z-spider splitting into a branch with a Hadamard and a branch with a triangle, merged by a Z-spider, equals a triangle followed by Z(π) (with a scalar).

axioms.label: (TR6)
axioms.description: A triangle, Z(π) and an upside-down triangle in sequence equal X(π) followed by a triangle.

axioms.label: (TR7)
axioms.description: A Z-spider and an X-spider joined by a plain branch and a branch with a triangle equal a single triangle (with a scalar).

axioms.label: (TR8)
axioms.description: A two-qubit identity commuting a triangle through a structure of Z-spiders and an X-spider.

axioms.label: (TR9)
axioms.description: A two-qubit identity involving triangles, an X-spider and Z-spiders, whose right-hand side contains a Hadamard and Z(π)-phases.

axioms.label: (TR10)
axioms.description: Two parallel triangles between two Z-spiders equal a single triangle.

axioms.label: (TR11)
axioms.description: Two inputs passing through a Z-spider and an X(π)-spider that are joined by a wire, then through triangles into a Z-spider, with a scalar, equal the two inputs passing through triangles into a Z-spider.

axioms.label: (TR12)
axioms.description: A Z-spider splitting into two branches with triangles, followed by a Z-spider and an X-spider joined by a wire (a CNOT), with a scalar, equals the Z-spider splitting into two branches with triangles.

axioms.label: (TR13)
axioms.description: Z(α) phases on both output legs of a structure made of an X-spider, Z-spiders and a triangle equal a single Z(α) on its input.

axioms.label: (TR14)
axioms.description: λ-boxes on both output legs of a structure made of an X-spider, Z-spiders and a triangle equal a single λ-box on its input.

results.title: Completeness for 2-qubit Clifford+T circuits
results.summary: The rules (S1), (S2), (B1), (B2), (H1), (H2), (N) and (P) make the ZX-calculus complete for 2-qubit Clifford+T circuits. All rules hold up to a non-zero scalar.

axioms.label: (S2)
axioms.note: The paper states the green and red versions in one rule; the stored rule is the Z-spider case.

axioms.label: (B1)
axioms.note: Stated without scalars.

axioms.label: (B2)
axioms.note: The paper ignores scalars.

axioms.label: (H1)
axioms.note: The paper ignores scalars (the stored rule has scalar e^{-iπ/4}).

axioms.label: (H2)
axioms.note: The paper writes Hadamard gates on the legs of one of the spiders; here they are Hadamard edges.

axioms.label: (N)
axioms.note: The paper's version is Z(α) followed by X(π) equals X(π) followed by Z(−α), on one wire and up to a scalar; the stored rule has two outputs and the colours swapped.

axioms.label: (P)
axioms.note: The paper only asserts that suitable β's exist (with a side condition relating α₂ and γ₂) and works up to scalars; the stored rule uses Vilmart's explicit formulas and is checked at one numerical instance.

results.title: Completeness for the single-qubit Clifford+T group
results.location: Section 2.1 (rules); Section 3, Theorems 5 and 8 (unique normal form)
results.summary: With the rules (Id), (S), (P), (C), (Eu) and their colour-swapped versions, every single-qubit Clifford+T diagram (one input, one output) rewrites to a unique normal form, so the ZX-calculus is complete for the single-qubit Clifford+T group. Equality is up to a global scalar.

axioms.label: (Id)
axioms.note: The paper allows a phase 2nπ, which is the same as 0.

axioms.label: (S)
axioms.note: The paper only uses the one-input one-output case.

axioms.label: (P)
axioms.note: The paper's version is on one wire (X(φ) then Z(π) equals Z(π) then X(−φ)), up to a scalar; the stored rule has two outputs and the colours swapped.

axioms.label: (C)
axioms.note: One-input one-output case: H Z(φ) H = X(φ), with Hadamard gates instead of Hadamard edges.

axioms.label: (Eu)
axioms.note: The paper ignores scalars (the stored rule has scalar e^{-iπ/4}).
